head: bf662f8
target: Ship the gate as one plugin that Claude Code, Droid, and Codex all load, with one installer, so every clone of an opted-in repo gets the gate at session start.
incidental: manifest field values in the plugin files
selftest rework: moved to the repo root, isolated home and git config, new hook tests
hook timeouts and the shell-tool matcher in the hooks file
the JSON shape of the guard's deny reply

questions.prompt: Before this change, the skill reached a repo as copied files. Why ship it as one plugin for Claude Code, Droid, and Codex?

options.label: The installer builds a package for each tool from the same source.
Claude Code and Droid share a layout, but Codex needs its hooks converted.
All three harnesses read the same plugin layout, so one copy serves them all.
A plugin can run hooks, but loose files in a repo cannot.

key_points: All three harnesses read the same plugin layout: one manifest and one hooks file.
One copy keeps the gate and the skill identical everywhere, with nothing to keep in sync.

questions.prompt: A teammate clones a repo that opted in. No session has run there yet. When does the push gate reach that clone?

options.label: On their first push, because git copies the hook from the repo's tracked files.
At their first session start, when the start hook syncs and installs the pre-push hook.
Right after the clone, because the opt-in marker carries the hook with it.
Never, because each clone needs a manual install of the gate.

key_points: At the first session start, the start hook runs the gate's sync, which installs the pre-push hook.
The opt-in marker travels with the repo; the hook arrives only with a session.
The start hook also tells the agent the repo is opted in.

questions.prompt: The agent wants to run each of these shell commands. Which ones does the guard deny?

options.label: A push told to skip the pre-push checks.
A commit told to skip the commit checks.
A config change to where git finds its hooks.
A config read of where git finds its hooks.

key_points: Denied: commands that push past the pre-push gate, or that move git's hooks away.
Allowed: reading the hooks path, and skipping commit-side checks, since neither reaches the remote.
The rule: skipping the gate is the human's call, never the agent's.

questions.prompt: A session starts where the gate cannot run. Say the sync fails, or the repo never opted in. What happens to the session?

options.label: The session start fails, and the hook is retried.
The session runs on. The start hook never fails a session.
The session warns the user and waits for a fix.
The session opens in a mode that blocks all pushes.

key_points: The session still starts: the start hook swallows the sync failure and stays quiet.
Outside a git repo, or without the opt-in marker, the hook prints nothing.

questions.prompt: Codex runs a plugin's hooks only after the user approves them in its own prompt. Why does the installer write the trust entries itself?

options.label: The approval prompt cannot appear when the installer runs from a script.
Untrusted hooks never run in Codex, so the gate would silently not exist.
The hook files change on every install, so old approvals never stick.
Codex forbids a plugin from adding hooks before its first session.

key_points: Codex skips a plugin's hooks until the user marks them trusted, without telling anyone.
The installer writes the same trust entries the Codex prompt would write on approval.
Running the installer counts as the human approving, and only this plugin's hooks are trusted.

questions.prompt: A repo opts in, but a teammate who never installed the plugin pushes to it from a plain terminal. What stops that push, and what does that show about the gate's reach?
key_points: Nothing stops that push: the gate lives in the clone's pre-push hook, which only a session with the plugin installs.
The opt-in marker asks agent sessions to enforce; it does not enforce at the remote.
The design gates work done with an agent; a human pushing by hand keeps full control.
